features.description: Repoint dashboard from `<axiom-firebase-project-id>` Firebase project to `<firebase-project-id>`. Update `axiom/packages/dashboard/app.js` `firebaseConfig` block. Switch from multi-tenant `tenants/{tenantId}/...` collection paths to single-tenant `projects/<project_id>/...` shape. Operator's local DontPanic project_id (from `~/.dontpanic/projects.json`) becomes the Firestore project_id segment.
steps: Update `firebaseConfig` constants in `app.js` to point at <firebase-project-id>.
Replace `tenantCollection(name)` and `tenantDoc(...)` helpers with `projectCollection(projectId, name)` / `projectDoc(projectId, ...)`.
Sub all five `subscribeAll()` listeners to the new path shape.
Smoke test: dashboard loads against <firebase-project-id> with at least one mock plan in Firestore.
features.acceptance: (1) `axiom/packages/dashboard/app.js` `firebaseConfig` references <firebase-project-id> (project_id, auth_domain, storage_bucket all correct). (2) Collection paths match `projects/<project_id>/<stream>` shape. (3) Dashboard loads and renders against a seed Firestore state.

features.description: Sync daemon — polls `dontpanic state snapshot --json --redact-level operator` and writes to Firestore. Runs locally on the operator's machine. Polling interval 5–15s configurable. Each stream maps to a Firestore collection: plans → `projects/{pid}/plans`, gates → `projects/{pid}/gates`, inbox → `projects/{pid}/activity`, supervisors → `projects/{pid}/agents`, quota → `projects/{pid}/metrics/tokens`, decisions → `projects/{pid}/decisions`. Idempotent upserts (use plan_id / gate_id / event_id as Firestore doc IDs).
steps: Create `axiom/packages/sync/dontpanic_sync.py` (or .ts) — polling daemon.
Implement diff-based upsert: compare incoming snapshot to last-written, only write changed docs.
Add a small CLI: `axiom-sync start [--interval 10] [--project-id <id>]`.
Tests cover the diff logic + idempotency + handling of `--include` projection responses.
Document running it as a launchd plist or systemd unit for persistent operation.
features.acceptance: (1) Daemon runs continuously; latency from local plan change to Firestore write ≤30s. (2) Idempotent — re-running same snapshot produces zero writes. (3) `--include` filters honored to skip heavy streams when the dashboard doesn't need them. (4) Tests cover diff, upsert, and failure paths.

features.description: Cloud Functions for state-changing dashboard actions. Three endpoints: `kanbanMove(planId, newColumn)` → maps the dashboard's column to a plan-status flip via DontPanic MCP `validate_plan` + the existing status-flip discipline. `approveGate(planId, gateName)` → DontPanic MCP `approve_gate` with `confirm: true`. `triggerDispatch(planId, featureId)` → DontPanic MCP `dispatch` with `confirm: true`. All three require operator auth via the dashboard's existing Firebase Auth integration. Functions run with credentials that can call the operator's local MCP via Tailscale Funnel or equivalent — operator chooses the bridge.
steps: Define Cloud Function signatures + auth requirements.
Implement the three callable functions using the existing Cloud Functions infra (`axiom/packages/functions/` or equivalent).
Resolve the local-MCP-from-Cloud-Function bridge — Tailscale Funnel is the recommended path; operator-side configuration documented separately.
Smoke test: call each function from the dashboard against a fixture plan, verify MCP was actually called.
features.acceptance: (1) Three Cloud Functions deployed and callable. (2) Each function calls DontPanic MCP — no direct Firestore mutation for state changes. (3) Auth required — unauthenticated calls rejected. (4) Smoke test passes end-to-end (dashboard click → Cloud Function → MCP → DontPanic state changes → sync daemon picks up → Firestore reflects → dashboard re-renders).

features.description: Firestore security rules. Read access requires authenticated operator. State-changing writes (anything in plans/gates/activity collections) DENIED for client-side calls — only Cloud Functions can write (via privileged service account). The sync daemon writes via service-account credentials too. Public/Observer-level access is intentionally NOT enabled in v0.
steps: Draft `firestore.rules` with auth-required read + service-account-only write.
Deploy rules and verify with the Firebase emulator.
Add a fixture test that asserts a client-side direct write is rejected.
features.acceptance: (1) `firestore.rules` deployed to <firebase-project-id>. (2) Authenticated reads work; client direct writes denied. (3) Fixture test enforces the deny.

features.description: End-to-end smoke test + operator runbook. Smoke test runs a synthetic plan through DontPanic locally, verifies the dashboard renders each stage (volley_start → gate_paused → approve via dashboard → signoff), and confirms latency stays under 30s per transition. Runbook documents how an operator stands up the adapter from scratch: Firebase project credentials, sync daemon launch, Cloud Function deploy, dashboard local serve.
steps: Author the synthetic plan + smoke-test script.
Run end-to-end against staging Firestore.
Capture screenshots / state snapshots as evidence.
Write `axiom/packages/dashboard/RUNBOOK.md` with the operator-side setup steps.
features.acceptance: (1) Smoke test passes; latency budgets met. (2) RUNBOOK exists and a fresh operator can follow it from blank Firebase project to working dashboard. (3) Evidence captured.
